fullPassage: Whether we feel happy or sad, content or discontent, is not determined merely by each individual successive moment of life experience — a good thing happens and I'm happy, a bad thing happens and I'm sad. While our experiences affect our mood, we are not blown in a completely new direction by each gust of wind. As humans, we adjust — to new information and events both good and bad — and return to our personal default level of well-being. There will be highs and lows, but over time, like water seeking its own level, we are pulled toward our baseline — back up after bad news and back down after good. The euphoria of first love fades, and so does the despair of a break-up. This tendency is best seen with little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they've longed for, they believe they will be happy for the rest of their lives. And for the first few minutes of the rest of their lives, they are. But then the kids — like adults — adapt.

❌ ② weakens(약해지다) — fades와 같은 '약화' 의미축
❌ ③ vanishes(사라지다) — fades와 동의어
❌ ④ disappears(사라지다) — fades와 동의어
det.tip: fade(사라지다) ↔ intensify(강해지다). 오답 ②③④는 fade와 같은 소멸·약화 의미

questions.passage: Whether we feel happy or sad, content or discontent, is not determined merely by each individual <u>successive</u> moment of life experience — a good thing happens and I'm happy, a bad thing happens and I'm sad. While our experiences affect our mood, we are not blown in a completely new direction by each gust of wind. As humans, we adjust — to new information and events both good and bad — and return to our personal default level of well-being. There will be highs and lows, but over time, like water seeking its own level, we are pulled toward our baseline — back up after bad news and back down after good. The euphoria of first love fades, and so does the despair of a break-up. This tendency is best seen with little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they've longed for, they believe they will be happy for the rest of their lives. And for the first few minutes of the rest of their lives, they are. But then the kids — like adults — adapt.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 successive와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: successive(연속적인) ↔ intermittent(간헐적인, 끊겼다 이어지는)
det.analysis:
❌ ① consecutive(연속적인) — successive와 동의어
✅ ② intermittent(간헐적인) — successive(연속적인)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ③ continuous(끊임없는) — successive와 같은 '연속' 의미축
❌ ④ frequent(잦은) — 빈도 의미로 '연속'의 반대는 아님
det.tip: successive(연이은) ↔ intermittent(간헐적인). consecutive·continuous는 오히려 동의어

questions.passage:
(A) Whether we feel happy or sad, <u>content</u> or discontent, our mood keeps shifting. A good thing happens and we feel great, while a bad thing brings us down.

(B) The magazine's <u>content</u> was rich and varied. It covered science, art, and history, so readers enjoyed every single page.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 content의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: content: (A) 만족한(형용사) — (B) 내용/콘텐츠(명사). 문맥에 따라 뜻이 달라지는 다의어
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 내용 — (B) 만족한: (A)는 happy/sad와 나란한 감정 형용사이므로 '만족한'
❌ ② (A) 담다 — (B) 내용: (A)는 동사가 아니라 형용사
✅ ③ (A) 만족한 — (B) 내용 — (A) happy or sad와 병렬된 '만족한', (B) 잡지에 실린 '내용' ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 만족한 — (B) 만족한: (B)는 잡지가 다룬 '내용(글감)'이지 감정이 아님
det.tip: content = 만족한(adj) / 내용(n). 품사·강세에 따라 뜻이 갈리는 다의어

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a sudden strong rush of wind"

det.korean: gust = 돌풍, 갑자기 강하게 부는 바람. 본문 'each gust of wind'
det.analysis:
❌ ① breeze(산들바람) — 약하고 부드러운 바람으로 'strong'과 불일치
❌ ② storm(폭풍) — 비·바람을 동반한 큰 기상 현상
❌ ③ drizzle(이슬비) — 바람이 아니라 약한 비
✅ ④ gust(돌풍) — 갑작스럽고 강한 바람 ←정답
det.tip: gust = 돌풍 (a sudden strong rush of wind). breeze(산들바람)와 강도가 다름

questions.passage: Whether we feel happy or sad, content or discontent, is not determined merely by each individual successive moment of life experience. While our __________ (experience) affect our mood, we are not blown in a completely new direction by each gust of wind.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: experience → experiences (복수명사). 동사 affect가 -s 없는 원형이므로 주어는 복수여야 한다
det.analysis: While our ___ affect our mood: 동사가 affect(3인칭 단수라면 붙어야 할 -s가 없는 형태)이므로 주어는 복수여야 한다. 따라서 experience를 복수형 experiences로 바꾼다. '우리의 경험들이 우리 기분에 영향을 준다'
det.tip: 동사 affect(원형·복수 일치) → 주어도 복수 → experience의 복수형 experiences

questions.passage: This tendency is best seen with little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they've __________ (long) for, they believe they will be happy for the rest of their lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: long → longed (현재완료 have + 과거분사). 'they've longed for' = 그들이 갈망해온
det.analysis: what they've longed for: 현재완료(have + 과거분사) 구문. they've(=they have) 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 하므로 long → longed. long for = ~을 갈망하다
det.tip: 현재완료 have + p.p. → they've longed for. long(규칙동사)의 과거분사는 longed

det.korean: 감정에는 '오르내림(highs and lows)'이 있지만 시간이 지나면 기준선으로 끌려간다
det.analysis:

det.korean: 우리는 각 '한 줄기 돌풍(gust of wind)'에 완전히 새 방향으로 날리지 않는다
det.analysis:
❌ ① ray of sun(햇살) — '날리다(blown)'와 어울리지 않음
✅ ② gust of wind(한 줄기 돌풍) — 바람에 완전히 새 방향으로 날리지 않는다는 비유 ←정답

❌ ④ grain of sand(모래 한 알) — 문맥 무관
det.tip: blown ... by each gust of wind = 바람 한 줄기에 휩쓸리다
